citation.authors: Reed JT, Ghadially R, Elias PM

record.population: 22-38 year-old White (8), Asian (6) adults; skin type II/III (14) against skin type V/VI (7)
record.design: Laboratory comparison of barrier strength (tape strips to disrupt barrier) and recovery
record.finding: Barrier function did not differ by race or sex. Skin type II/III needed 29.6 tape strips to disrupt the barrier against 66.7 for skin type V/VI, and V/VI recovered faster (43% against about 20% at 6 hours). The authors conclude skin type, not race, influences barrier function.
record.note: Very small. The abstract lists White and Asian groups for race comparisons; the V/VI group's ancestry is not given. This is the example for the measured-variable rule.
